At test time, DREAM-Chunk samples multiple candidate action chunks, rolls out their predicted latent futures, and selects actions from the chunk whose predicted state best matches the observed rollout. In this way, DREAM-Chunk uses additional test-time computation to cover multiple plausible stochastic futures and improve reactivity during long-horizon chunk execution. On the Kinetix benchmark, DREAM-Chunk improves robustness under increasing action noise and benefits from larger candidate sample sizes, especially when demonstrations contain corrective behaviors. We further validate DREAM-Chunk on four manipulation tasks across two robot platforms and two VLA policies under various sources of stochasticity. Across simulation and hardware experiments, DREAM-Chunk improves the robustness of action-chunking policies in stochastic dynamics.

</details>


### [150] [Benchmarking Action Spaces in Reinforcement Learning for Vision-based Robotic Manipulation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18594)
*Seyed Alireza Azimi,Homayoon Farrahi,Abhishek Naik,Colin Bellinger,A. Rupam Mahmood*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: The study examines how different action spaces in reinforcement learning impact task performance in real-world manipulation tasks and finds that joint velocity representation offers the best outcomes.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Understanding the influence of action space choices in reinforcement learning could improve the smoothness and safety of robot movements, enhancing performance in real-world applications.

Method: The study evaluates different action spaces (pose increment, pose velocity, joint position increment, joint velocity) in simulation-based training, followed by sim-to-real deployment to assess performance in object manipulation tasks.

Result: Joint velocity action space significantly outperformed other representations in terms of motion smoothness and task success for the vision-based picking and pushing tasks.

Conclusion: Choosing the appropriate action space is crucial for effective sim-to-real transfer in reinforcement learning, and joint velocity is recommended for enhanced performance.

Abstract: In real-world reinforcement learning (RL), the choice of action space can play a key role in shaping motion smoothness, safety, and overall task performance. In this study, we evaluate pose increment, pose velocity, joint position increment, and joint velocity across two vision-based manipulation tasks: object picking and pushing. We train policies in simulation and deploy them to the real world using sim-to-real transfer. We find that action-space representation indeed significantly affects sim-to-real performance. In particular, we find that the joint velocity action space is best for the vision-based picking and pushing tasks in terms of smoothness and final task performance. We also provide practical guidance for RL practitioners in choosing action spaces for both simulation and real-world experiments.

</details>


### [151] [Admittance-Based Surface Alignment for Human-in-the-Loop Robotic Visual Inspection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18601)
*Antara Banerjee,Colin Acton,Xu Chen*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: This paper presents a novel real-time robotic orientation control system for precision visual inspection that combines operator input with perception-driven alignment to enhance quality assurance in manufacturing.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: The need for precise robotic visual inspection in high-value manufacturing environments highlights the need for control architectures that can adapt to human input and perceptual uncertainties.

Method: The paper proposes an admittance-based framework that allows for reactive and compliant orientation control, treating the end-effector as a virtual sphere in a viscous medium to achieve smooth motion.

Result: The proposed control pipeline was validated on a 6-DOF manipulator, achieving stable normal-tracking with a mean orientation error of 0.4°.

Conclusion: The framework successfully integrates operator commands and perception feedback, improving the effectiveness of robotic inspection systems in complex industrial settings.

Abstract: Precision visual inspection underpins quality assurance across aerospace, semiconductor, and medical manufacturing, where undetected surface anomalies on high-value parts translate directly into scrap, rework, and field failures. Robotic visual inspection requires precise alignment between the end-effector and local surface geometry in the presence of perception noise and surface irregularities. In industrial settings, a human operator is often kept in the loop via teleoperation or shared autonomy, introducing real-time adjustments that render purely offline motion planning inadequate. This motivates control architectures capable of reactive, compliant behavior under combined human and perceptual uncertainty. This paper presents a novel real-time, closed-loop robotic orientation control pipeline for precision visual inspection, with an admittance-based framework that unifies operator input and perception-driven surface alignment. We design the end-effector as a virtual sphere moving through a viscous medium, such that the resulting physically interpretable mass--damper system generates synchronized, compliant motion from orientation error and operator commands. We validate the framework on a 6-DOF manipulator demonstrating stable normal-tracking and a final mean orientation error of 0.4°.

</details>


### [152] [SC3-Eval: Evaluating Robot Foundation Models via Self-Consistent Video Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18610)
*Wei-Cheng Tseng,Gashon Hussein,Yuzhu Dong,Allen Z. Ren,Lucy X. Shi,XuDong Wang,Sergey Levine,Zhaoshuo Li,Jinwei Gu,Florian Shkurti,Ming-Yu Liu,Quan Vuong*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: SC3-Eval proposes a novel video generation approach to evaluate robot manipulation policies by enforcing consistency across dynamics, views, and testing, significantly improving performance over prior models.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To enhance the evaluation of generalist robot manipulation policies efficiently and effectively, addressing existing challenges in scaling simulations and error accumulation.

Method: SC3-Eval utilizes a self-consistent video generation framework that incorporates forward-inverse dynamics, cross-view consistency, and test-time consistency to ensure coherent and accurate policy evaluation.

Result: SC3-Eval achieved a Pearson correlation of 0.929 and MMRV of 0.119 across seven real-world policies, outperforming three existing video-model baselines and exhibiting effective generalization to new tasks.

Conclusion: The self-consistent approach provides better diagnostics and reliable evaluations for complex robot manipulation tasks, enabling a deeper understanding of policy performance.

Abstract: Evaluating generalist robot manipulation policies in the real world is expensive, slow, and difficult to scale. Action-conditioned video world models offer a scalable alternative by simulating policy rollouts. Autoregressive rollouts accumulate compounding errors, observations across multiple camera views must remain mutually consistent, and the evaluator must generalize to policies whose behaviors lie outside the training distribution. We address these challenges with SC3-Eval, a self-consistent video generation recipe that adapts a pre-trained video foundation model into an accurate policy evaluator by enforcing three complementary forms of consistency. First, forward-inverse dynamics consistency jointly trains the model to predict frames from actions and to recover actions from frames, anchoring generated rollouts to a physically plausible action manifold and counteracting the drift a forward-only model cannot penalize. Second, cross-view consistency trains the model to inpaint each camera view from the other, keeping the multi-camera observation coherent over long rollouts without any explicit memory mechanism. Third, test-time consistency reuses the inverse dynamics mode at inference as a per-action-chunk uncertainty signal that terminates rollouts whose generated frames drift away from the requested actions. We also demonstrate SC3-Eval rollouts reproduce the failure modes that policies exhibit in real-world rollouts, supporting fine-grained diagnostic comparison rather than aggregate ranking alone. Across seven real-world vision-language-action policies, SC3-Eval attains a closed-loop Pearson correlation of $0.929$ and MMRV of $0.119$, outperforming three strong prior video-model-based baselines, and generalizes to new tasks.

</details>


### [153] [SRL: Combining SLIP Model and Reinforcement Learning for Agile Robotic Jumping](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18625)
*Xiaowen Hu,Linqi Ye,Yudi Zhu,Chenyue Shao,Rankun Li,Qingdu Li,Yan Peng*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: The paper proposes a hybrid framework called Spring-loaded Reinforcement Learning (SRL) that combines the Spring-Loaded Inverted Pendulum model with Reinforcement Learning to enhance robotic jumping performance over irregular terrain with improved stability and reduced training time.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: The need for efficient robotic jumping in critical applications is hindered by the limitations of existing models like SLIP on irregular terrain and RL's data-intensive nature.

Method: The proposed SRL framework integrates SLIP-based feedforward control with RL-driven real-time feedback for continuous optimization of jumping performance.

Result: Experimental results show that SRL achieves stable jumps with significantly less training time, maintaining tracking errors below specified thresholds.

Conclusion: SRL demonstrates robust adaptability across various simulations and real-world validations, indicating its potential for practical application in complex environments.

Abstract: Robotic jumping is pivotal in applications such as search and rescue and logistics, where crossing obstacles and enhancing mobility efficiency are critical. The Spring-Loaded Inverted Pendulum (SLIP) model leverages simplified spring-mass dynamics that naturally encode biologically plausible hopping motions, yet its performance degrades on irregular terrain due to idealized assumptions regarding contact and joint dynamics. Meanwhile, Reinforcement Learning (RL) can adapt to diverse and complex environments but often requires extensive data from unguided exploration. The complementary strengths of SLIP's physically grounded baseline and RL's adaptive capabilities motivate a hybrid framework that overcomes these individual limitations. We therefore propose Spring-loaded Reinforcement Learning (SRL), which integrates SLIP-based feedforward control signals with RL-driven real-time feedback, enabling continuous optimization of robotic jumping. Experimental results demonstrate that SRL can achieve more stable jumps with much less training time than the baseline method, maintaining an average position tracking error below 0.1 m and velocity tracking errors within +/-3% of the target values. Through bipedal and quadrupedal simulations of ground and stair jumping, as well as sim-to-sim and sim-to-real validations, SRL exhibits robust adaptability to various task requirements and environmental complexities, underscoring its potential for real-world deployment.

</details>


### [154] [Self-Supervised Mask-Aware Transformers for Fault-Tolerant FBG Force Sensing in Minimally Invasive Surgical Robotics](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18628)
*Peibo Sun,Shiyuan Dong,Shucheng Ye,Jianrong Cai,Yushan Liu,Hongen Liao,Tianqi Huang,Fang Chen*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: This paper presents a self-supervised mask-aware Transformer for stress estimation in catheter-scale Fiber Bragg Grating sensors, addressing challenges of channel dropouts and nonlinear cross-axis coupling in minimally invasive surgical robotics.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: The aim is to improve force estimation accuracy in minimally invasive surgery using Fiber Bragg Grating sensors, which face issues such as channel dropouts and nonlinearity.

Method: A unified, self-supervised mask-aware Transformer is proposed, pretrained for channel reconstruction and fine-tuned for force regression, incorporating uncertainty prediction per-axis.

Result: The model achieves an RMSE of 0.0066 N and maintains performance of 0.0126 N under severe channel loss, outperforming traditional model bank approaches.

Conclusion: The proposed approach enables efficient and reliable force estimation in the presence of sensor failures without the need for extensive calibration.

Abstract: In minimally invasive surgical robotics, catheter-scale Fiber Bragg Grating (FBG) sensors are promising due to their ability to estimate multi-dimensional forces by multiplexing several optical channels. However, deploying these compact multi-channel sensors introduces two critical engineering challenges: inherent nonlinear cross-axis coupling during complex deformations, and intermittent channel dropouts caused by fiber fractures in constrained workspaces. These compounding issues severely degrade force estimation. Existing fault-tolerant approaches rely on combinatorial model banks, which scale exponentially with the channel count and demand prohibitively expensive per-pattern calibration. In this paper, we propose a unified, self-supervised mask-aware Transformer that explicitly models channel availability to enable graceful degradation under diverse and dynamic sensor failures. The encoder is pretrained via masked-channel reconstruction on unlabeled data streams and fine-tuned for force regression using a balanced clean-and-corrupted-view objective alongside a dynamic corruption curriculum. Furthermore, a parallel uncertainty head, trained via heteroscedastic Gaussian negative log-likelihood, predicts per-axis confidence in a single forward pass, circumventing the overhead of multi-pass ensembles. Evaluated on a catheter-scale 8-channel FBG dataset, our single unified model achieves a nominal Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 0.0066~N and degrades gracefully to 0.0126~N under severe 4-channel failures. This significantly outperforms a comprehensive model bank of 255 per-pattern neural networks (0.0154~N at 4-channel loss) while eliminating pattern-specific calibration.

</details>


### [155] [DNN Koopman-Based Deviation Compensation for UGV Path Tracking Control on Coupled Slope and Potholed Road](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18630)
*Jian Zhao,Wenbo Zhou,Zhicheng Chen,Bing Zhu,Jiayi Han,Dongjian Song,Yinju Lin,Peixing Zhang*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: This paper presents a novel DNN Koopman-based strategy to enhance path tracking control of unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs) in complex terrains, achieving over 11.5% improvement in tracking performance.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: UGVs face significant challenges in maintaining path tracking accuracy due to complex terrain disturbances, particularly in off-road scenarios.

Method: The proposed method utilizes a DNN Koopman-based deviation compensation strategy, involving an adaptive recursive least squares method for estimating tire cornering stiffness, Laguerre model predictive control for efficient path tracking, and an event-triggered parallel cooperative mechanism for compensation.

Result: The experimental results indicate improved path tracking performance by more than 11.5% across various operating conditions when the proposed strategy is applied.

Conclusion: The integration of advanced computational techniques significantly enhances UGV path tracking accuracy and stability in challenging environments.

Abstract: Unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs) operating in off-road scenarios are confronted with complex terrain disturbances that can substantially degrade path tracking performance. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a deep neural network (DNN) Koopman-based deviation compensation strategy for UGV path tracking control. Firstly, based on the vehicle dynamic function on coupled slope, an adaptive forgetting recursive least squares method with decoupled error terms is designed to estimate tire cornering stiffness. On this basis, a Laguerre model predictive control (LMPC) path tracking control strategy is designed by incorporating Laguerre functions, which can reduce computational resource usage while maintaining reliable tracking performance across different coupled slope scenarios. Then, by integrating Koopman operator theory with DNN, a DNN Koopman (DK) path deviation compensation method is proposed, which significantly improves the path tracking accuracy of UGV under potholed road disturbances. Furthermore, an event-triggered parallel cooperative (EPC) compensation mechanism that couples LMPC with DK is established based on compensation activation criteria and credibility verification. This mechanism improves path tracking accuracy on potholed road while ensuring the feasibility of overall steering command and stability of vehicle after DK compensation. Finally, a hardware-in-the-loop (HiL) experimental platform is constructed for validation. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed UGV path tracking strategy improves tracking performance by more than 11.5% across multiple operating conditions.

</details>


### [156] [ROBOSHACKLES: A Safety Dataset for Human-Injury Prevention in Embodied Foundation Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18632)
*Zhuowen Yin,Chongyang Liu,Wenzhang Yang,Renjue Li,Yinxing Xue*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: The paper presents a pipeline for constructing a dataset aimed at improving the safety alignment of Embodied Foundation Models (EFMs) with respect to human-injury prevention, addressing the ethical challenges of collecting real-world data on robot harm.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To enhance the safety of robots in household settings and prevent human injuries, which remains a critical but underexplored area in the development of EFMs.

Method: The authors developed a safety-critical data construction pipeline that utilizes real DROID observations, incorporating scene understanding, hazard-aware editing, temporal prompt generation, and single-pass rollout synthesis to produce the ROBOSHACKLES dataset.

Result: The resultant ROBOSHACKLES dataset consists of 10,000 robotic video clips categorized into direct and indirect harm, revealing that evaluated EFMs generated unsafe actions at a 100% rate in safety-critical scenarios.

Conclusion: The findings underscore the need for improved safety measures in EFMs and present ROBOSHACKLES as an essential resource for future research in refusal learning and hazard anticipation during robotic actions.

Abstract: Embodied Foundation Models (EFMs) integrate multimodal understanding, future-state reasoning, and executable robot actions. Yet their safety alignment for human-injury prevention remains underexplored, primarily because real-world data of robots harming humans or creating hazardous household situations cannot be safely or ethically collected. To address this challenge, we propose a safety-critical data construction pipeline for human-injury prevention in EFMs.Starting from real DROID observations, our construction pipeline proceeds through scene understanding, hazard-aware image editing, temporal prompt generation, and single-pass rollout synthesis. The temporal prompts specify the expected scene evolution, while Wan2.7 synthesizes realistic robotic rollouts from the edited hazardous states in a single pass. Using this pipeline, we construct ROBOSHACKLES, a 10,000-clip robotic video dataset derived from real DROID observations, spanning two direct-harm and four indirect-harm categories. To ensure dataset quality, we assess task completion and visual quality with automatic metrics, and evaluate six representative EFMs under a refusal-based safety criterion. Results show that all evaluated models produce unsafe actions in the tested safety-critical scenarios, yielding a 100% unsafe action generation rate. ROBOSHACKLES serves as a scalable benchmark and training resource for refusal learning and hazard anticipation before robot action execution.The dataset is publicly available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/YZW00/RoboShackles.

</details>


### [157] [EffiNav: Fusing Depth and Vision-Language for Efficient Object Goal Navigation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18634)
*Zecheng Yin,Benedict Jun Ma*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: EffiNav improves object goal navigation efficiency and generalization in autonomous agents, outperforming traditional models on benchmark tests and in real-world applications.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To enhance autonomous agents' navigation efficiency in unknown environments for applications like search-and-rescue and field robots.

Method: EffiNav framework evaluated on simulation benchmarks and physical robots, with extensions to memory-augmented ObjNav tasks.

Result: EffiNav matches or surpasses recent baselines in Success Rate and Success weighted by Path Length across key evaluation metrics.

Conclusion: EffiNav demonstrates balanced performance and better generalizability for efficient object goal navigation.

Abstract: To locate a target object while exploring the unknown environment is a fundamental capability for autonomous agents, with applications ranging from search-and-rescue to field robots. A simplified version of such task is Object Goal Navigation (ObjNav). In ObjNav, successful arrival at the target object provides a basic measure of performance; however, the efficiency of the navigation trajectory is equally important, as it indicates how intelligently the agent explores and how much time remains for subsequent tasks. In unknown environments, the key to efficient navigation lies in deciding where to explore next. While many prior works aim to address this core challenge and achieved promising performance in certain settings, recent training-based models and non-training frameworks still suffer from generalization and efficiency issues respectively, which in the worst cases can lead to excessive exploration of already-visited areas or redundant back-and-forth motion. We evaluate EffiNav on two widely used simulation benchmarks Habitat Matterport 3D (HM3D) and Open-Vocabulary Object goal Navigation (OVON), and further validate its effectiveness on physical robots in real-world settings. We conduct failure analysis on massive simulation episodes. With minimal modification, we also extend EffiNav to a memory-augmented ObjNav task on the GOAT-BENCH dataset, demonstrating its adaptability beyond standard ObjNav settings. Across two standard metrics--Success Rate (SR) and Success weighted by Path Length (SPL), EffiNav matches or outperforms recent baselines, reflecting its efficiency, robustness, and practical applicability. Recognizing the different emphases of the two datasets, the performances reveals this framework is more balanced and generalizable for efficient ObjNav.

</details>


### [158] [A Scalable Embodied Intelligence Platform for Seamless Real-to-Sim-to-Real Transfer of Household Mobile Manipulation Tasks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18646)
*Kui Yang,Xianlei Long,Haoxuan Li,Yan Ding,Chao Chen*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: BestMan is a new platform designed to improve real-to-sim-to-real transfer in mobile manipulation robotics, overcoming challenges in simulation and deployment.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: The need for effective, robust mobile manipulation in unstructured household environments necessitates advancements in embodied intelligence platforms to enhance the real-to-sim-to-real cycle.

Method: BestMan incorporates an Automated Scene Generation (ASG) module for realistic simulation reconstruction, a simulation-guided architecture for skill learning and task formalization, and a Hardware-agnostic and Unified Middleware (HUM) for compatibility across mobile manipulators.

Result: Experimental results indicate that BestMan significantly improves real-to-sim-to-real transfers and establishes standardized benchmarks for mobile manipulation.

Conclusion: BestMan effectively bridges the simulation and real-world gap, promoting further research and development in household mobile manipulation robotics.

Abstract: Mobile manipulation is a fundamental capability in embodied intelligence robotics. The growing demand for robust and generalizable manipulation in unstructured household environments has driven rapid progress in embodied intelligence platforms. However, achieving a seamless transfer across the real-to-sim-to-real cycle faces three key challenges, including costly high-fidelity simulation scenes reconstruction, the complexity of systematic strategy evaluation in simulation, and incompatible real-world deployments. To address these challenges, we develop BestMan, a scalable and seamless real-to-sim-to-real platform that bridges the gap between the simulation and the real world, enabling effective strategy development, integration, and deployment for household mobile manipulation. Specifically, we design a novel Automated Scene Generation (ASG) module to reconstruct realistic simulations from real observations. Then, we propose a simulation-guided task formalization and skill learning architecture that supports the flexible integration and large-scale evaluations of hybrid skill strategies in simulation. Finally, to enhance the real-world scalability, we develop a Hardware-agnostic and Unified Middleware (HUM) to ensure seamless and compatible sim-to-real transfer across heterogeneous mobile manipulators for real deployments. Experimental results demonstrate the superior performance of our proposed platform in establishing standardized benchmarks and facilitating promising research in the field of mobile manipulation.

</details>


### [159] [High-Degree-of-Freedom Lightweight Bioinspired Leg for Enhanced Mobility in Small Robots](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18680)
*Haoqi Han,Yifei Yu,Jiaming Zhang,Xinru Cui,Linxi Feng,Hesheng Wang*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: This paper introduces a novel micro-scale leg mechanism inspired by insect locomotion, designed for microrobotics with enhanced flexibility and reduced inertia.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: The need to improve locomotion capabilities in microrobotics while operating under strict spatial constraints.

Method: A micro-scale parallel leg mechanism with four DoF is developed, utilizing spherical five-bar linkages for improved kinematics and a concentric design to streamline analysis.

Result: The mechanism has a total mass of 18.9 g, capable of generating an output force of approximately 0.5 N, with a workspace of over 22255 mm3, and exhibits excellent motion flexibility in experiments.

Conclusion: This innovative leg mechanism shows promise for advanced applications in micro bio-inspired robotics, given its lightweight design and functional capabilities.

Abstract: In microrobotics, enhancing locomotion capabilities by increasing the degrees of freedom (DoF) of leg mechanisms under severe spatial constraints remains a significant challenge. Inspired by insect locomotion, this paper presents a novel micro-scale parallel leg mechanism with four degrees of freedom, and systematically analyzes its mechanical design, electrical system, and kinematics. The design incorporates two spherical five-bar linkages to achieve spatial motion within a parallel four-bar configuration. Furthermore, a concentric design strategy is employed to simplify the analytical solution of the leg kinematics. Due to the parallel system architecture, all actuators are located on the main body, substantially reducing the equivalent inertia of moving parts compared to traditional high-DOF leg structures. The total mass of the system is only 18.9 g, with an end-effector output force of approximately 0.5 N and a workspace exceeding 22255 mm3. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed single-leg mechanism achieves excellent motion flexibility, highlighting its potential for micro bio-inspired robotics.

</details>


### [160] [Leveraging Energy Features for Surface Classification with Deep Learning: A Comparative Analysis Across Three Independent Datasets](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18698)
*Alexander Belyaev,Oleg Kushnarev*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: The study assesses energy-based features for surface classification in mobile robotics, highlighting their effectiveness alone and in conjunction with inertial data.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To explore the potential of energy-derived features in surface classification, an area that has not been thoroughly investigated despite intriguing results in limited settings.

Method: Evaluation of energy features as a standalone classification modality and as supplementary inputs to inertial data across three public datasets using various deep learning architectures, including automated hyperparameter tuning and optimization.

Result: Modern architectures outperformed previous reports, with convolutional neural networks achieving the highest performance. Energy-only models reached 85-90% accuracy, while combining energy with inertial features resulted in 96-99% accuracy, with a 1-2% mean improvement.

Conclusion: Energy-based features can be effectively used for classification on their own and provide added accuracy when combined with inertial data.

Abstract: The energy-based method remains a comparatively underexamined approach for surface classification in mobile robotics, despite promising results in constrained environments. This study evaluated the viability of using energy-derived features as either a standalone classification modality or as supplementary input to inertial data. A comprehensive evaluation was conducted across three publicly available datasets, comparing the performance of modern deep learning architectures including recurrent neural networks, convolutional neural networks, encoder-only transformers, and Mamba state-space models, under automated hyperparameter tuning and input sequence length optimization. The models achieved higher accuracy than previously reported values on all evaluated datasets, with the convolutional neural network yielding the highest overall performance. When relying exclusively on energy-based features, the models attained classification accuracies in the range of 85-90%, approximately 5-10% lower than those achieved when combined with inertial features (96-99%). Augmenting inertial data with energy features resulted in a consistent mean accuracy improvement of 1-2%. These findings indicate that classifiers relying solely on energy features offer sufficient accuracy for standalone deployment, while also providing a consistent gain when used in combination with other sensing modalities.

</details>


### [161] [Selective Unit-Cell Actuation in Lattice Structures for Distributed Morphology in Soft Robots](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18704)
*Trevor Exley,Altair Coutinho,Lucia Beccai*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: The paper introduces a novel design for soft lattice structures that integrates actuation at the unit-cell scale using pneumatic mechanisms, enabling versatile deformation for soft robotics applications.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To enhance the compliance and deformation capabilities of soft lattice structures in robotics by integrating actuation directly into the unit-cell design.

Method: An embedded pneumatic unit cell combining curved-strut lattice geometry with a bidirectional bellow actuator is developed, allowing for spatially controlled actuation when tessellated.

Result: Experimental tests on various tessellations showed scalable performance in displacement and force generation, with selective actuation demonstrating distinct global deformation modes such as bending and grasping.

Conclusion: Unit-cell-level actuation provides a promising approach for distributed morphing in soft robots, paving the way for advanced, scalable robotic architectures.

Abstract: Soft lattice structures are increasingly used in robotics to tailor compliance and guide deformation; however, actuation is typically introduced at the device or module level, with actuators inserted into otherwise passive architectures. In this work, we move actuator-lattice co-design to the unit-cell scale. We present an embedded pneumatic unit cell that integrates curved-strut lattice geometry with a bidirectional bellow actuator within a single monolithic element. When tessellated, the lattice functions as a distributed actuation field in which global morphology is governed by spatial actuation patterns rather than uniform pressurization. Experimental characterization of 1x1, 2x2, and 3x3 tessellations demonstrates scalable displacement and force generation with repeatable cyclic performance. Selective actuation of unit cells in a 3x3x3 array produces distinct global deformation modes, including bending and directional grasping, without altering hardware configuration. Additionally, coupling active and passive unit cells enables bending-driven crawling locomotion, demonstrating that heterogeneous tessellations can translate through asymmetric deformation. These results establish unit-cell-level actuation as a strategy for distributed morphing in lattice-based soft robots and provide a foundation for scalable, monolithic robotic architectures.

</details>


### [162] [Two-Phase Bilevel Search for the Moving-Target Traveling Salesman Problem with Moving Obstacles](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18730)
*Allen George Philip,Anoop Bhat,Sivakumar Rathinam,Howie Choset*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: Study on the MT-TSP-MO presents effective algorithms for optimal agent trajectories avoiding moving obstacles.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To optimize trajectory planning in scenarios where agents must navigate to moving targets while avoiding dynamic obstacles.

Method: Utilizes Mixed-Integer Conic Programming and Two-Phase Bilevel Search for solution computation.

Result: Proposed methods surpass baseline in success rates, solution costs, and computation time across various instances.

Conclusion: The developed algorithms provide efficient solutions for the complex MT-TSP-MO problem.

Abstract: The Moving-Target Traveling Salesman Problem (MT-TSP) seeks a minimum cost trajectory for an agent that departs from a static depot, visits a set of moving targets, each within one of their assigned time windows, and returns to the depot. In this article, we study the Moving-Target Traveling Salesman Problem with Moving Obstacles (MT-TSP-MO), a generalization of the MT-TSP where the agent trajectory must avoid moving obstacles. We present a Mixed-Integer Conic Programming (MICP) formulation that can be solved using off-the-shelf solvers, as well as a fast and scalable Two-Phase Bilevel Search (TPBS) algorithm that computes high-quality feasible solutions for the problem. We evaluate our approaches against an existing baseline algorithm on a broad range of problem instances with up to 40 targets and 40 obstacles. The results demonstrate that both the proposed methods significantly outperform the baseline with respect to success rates, solution costs, and computation time.

</details>


### [163] [Generating Natural and Expressive Robot Gestures through Iterative Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback using LLMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18747)
*Chris Lee,Flora Salim,Benjamin Tag,Francisco Cruz*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: This paper explores using machine learning and reinforcement learning with human feedback (RLHF) to enhance gesture generation for the humanoid robot Pepper, integrating ChatGPT for improved co-speech gestures.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: The motivation is to improve human-robot interaction (HRI) by enabling the humanoid robot Pepper to produce natural and expressive gestures that adapt to dynamic environments while adhering to social norms.

Method: The study integrates ChatGPT for dynamic code generation of gestures, then enhances this with iterative reinforcement learning based on human feedback to finetune gesture quality.

Result: The application of RLHF significantly improved the perceived quality of Pepper's gestures, making them more expressive and fluid compared to initial results from ChatGPT alone.

Conclusion: The findings indicate that iterative refinement using human evaluations can effectively enhance robot gesture generation, contributing to better HRI and acceptance of social robots.

Abstract: Expressive gestures are essential for natural and effective communication, complementing speech when verbal cues alone are insufficient (e.g., pointing). For social robots such as the humanoid Pepper, producing natural and expressive movements is critical for improving human-robot interaction (HRI) and long-term acceptance. However, generating gestures remains challenging due to reliance on expert-authored animations, resulting in rigid behaviors that are impractical for dynamic and diverse environments. Alternatively, machine learning approaches often struggle to capture perceived naturalness, becoming increasingly challenging with more degrees of freedom. Consequently, producing expressive robot gestures requires a system that can adapt to the environment while adhering to social norms and physical constraints. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) enable dynamic code generation, offering new opportunities for runtime gesture synthesis from natural language. In this paper, we integrate ChatGPT into the humanoid robot Pepper to generate co-speech gestures aligned with conversational output. While this baseline enables flexible gesture generation, the resulting motions are often perceived as stiff and unnatural. To address this limitation, we introduce an iterative reinforcement learning with human feedback (RLHF) system that finetunes gesture generation based on user evaluations, leveraging an iterative user study to compare Pepper's generated gestures. Our results show that RLHF improved the LLM's co-speech generative capabilities, producing more expressive, relevant and fluid movements.

</details>


### [164] [HALOMI: Learning Humanoid Loco-Manipulation with Active Perception from Human Demonstrations](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18772)
*Zehui Zhao,Yuxuan Zhao,Gaojing Zhang,Chenxi Liu,Maolin Zheng,Wenzhao Lian*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: HALOMI is a scalable framework that utilizes human demonstrations for humanoid loco-manipulation, addressing challenges in precise tracking and human-to-humanoid gaps.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To effectively leverage human demonstrations for humanoid robots in loco-manipulation tasks, while overcoming limitations in tracking and adaptability to humanoid operations.

Method: HALOMI integrates egocentric sensing for improved observation collection and employs a manifold-constrained controller for robust tracking and execution.

Result: HALOMI achieves an average success rate of 85% on quantitative tasks and demonstrates additional capabilities in dynamic behaviors.

Conclusion: HALOMI effectively bridges the gap between human and humanoid performance in loco-manipulation, showcasing potential for complex robotic tasks.

Abstract: Human demonstrations, which can be collected at scale and naturally capture active hand-eye coordination, are a promising data source for learning humanoid loco-manipulation. However, directly transferring human demonstrations to humanoids requires a precise world-frame tracking controller, which is often brittle under Out-of-Distribution(OOD) targets, while human-to-humanoid gaps persist in both egocentric observation and action execution. To address these challenges, we present HALOMI, a scalable framework for learning humanoid loco-manipulation with active perception from human demonstrations. HALOMI extends Universal Manipulation Interface (UMI) with egocentric sensing to collect ego-view and wrist-view observations along with head-hand trajectories at scale. We further propose a manifold-constrained controller that plans in a learned latent behavior manifold to enable precise and robust head-hand tracking in the world frame. To bridge the human-to-humanoid gap, we perform ego-view alignment and introduce a controller-aware reference trajectory adaptation to reduce mismatch in both observation and action execution. We validate HALOMI on a Unitree G1 humanoid robot with an actuated neck across five real-world tasks involving navigation, grasping, bimanual manipulation, whole-body coordination, and dynamic behaviors. Across the three quantitatively evaluated tasks, HALOMI achieves an average success rate of 85\%, while additional qualitative demonstrations show its ability to support dynamic tossing and deep-squat grasping.

</details>


### [165] [Space Is Intelligence: Neural Semigroup Superposition for Riemannian Metric Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18828)
*Chenghao Xu*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: This paper proposes a novel framework for navigating environments by embedding intelligence within the configuration space through a Riemannian metric, rather than in the agent itself, achieving effective, robust path planning via an Encoder-Router network.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To overcome limitations of traditional intelligence-based planning in agents by shifting the source of intelligence to the environment, allowing for seamless navigation based on the scene's geometry.

Method: The proposed approach uses an Encoder-Router network with three parameter groups to create a Riemannian metric field. This encapsulates the spatial characteristics of the environment, enabling path planning through geodesic following.

Result: The model, trained on a two-obstacle scene, exhibits zero-shot generalization to new obstacle configurations, showing significant differences in path costs between collision-free and obstacle-penetrating routes.

Conclusion: By integrating intelligence within the environmental space and employing a compact architecture for path planning, this approach enhances the adaptability and efficiency of navigation in varying obstacle arrangements.

Abstract: Traditional approaches place intelligence in the agent, whether as a learned policy or a search procedure. We instead place intelligence in the space itself: a scene induces a Riemannian metric on the configuration manifold, and action reduces to following the geodesics of that metric rather than invoking a separate planner or collision checker. A single Encoder-Router network realizes this idea through three complementary parameter groups -- frame parameters that orient the generators, modulation parameters that govern their spatial propagation, and basic coefficients that determine their strength. These groups combine through a shared semigroup-superposition mechanism to produce a single Riemannian metric field, yielding a compact architecture whose geometry scales naturally with scene complexity. Trained on a single two-obstacle scene, the model demonstrates robust zero-shot generalization across unseen obstacle configurations, with orders-of-magnitude separation between collision-free and obstacle-penetrating path costs.

</details>


### [166] [ZiMPedance: Impedance-Aware ZMP Modeling and Control for Payload Carrying with Quadruped Robots](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18883)
*Giovanni B. Dessy,Lorenzo Amatucci,Victor Barasuol,Claudio Semini*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: This paper explores the dynamics of load transportation in quadruped robots using passive spring-based arms, presenting a Modified ZMP approach to improve stability and efficiency in locomotion.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: The motivation is to improve stability and efficiency in quadruped robots during load transportation by addressing the dynamics of the physical interface between the robot and the load.

Method: The method involves deriving an extended Zero Moment Point (ZMP) formulation that incorporates passive payload-interface dynamics, augmenting a Single Rigid Body Dynamics model with passive dynamics, and integrating this model into a Model Predictive Control framework.

Result: Simulation results show a reduction in stability violations by up to 10 times and a 15% decrease in horizontal ground reaction force, compared to a baseline. Hardware experiments confirm stable locomotion with a 2 kg payload under disturbances where traditional methods fail.

Conclusion: The proposed approach enhances locomotion stability and efficiency in quadruped robots, enabling effective load transportation without requiring direct arm actuation.

Abstract: Load transportation with quadruped robots is strongly affected by the dynamics of the physical interface between the robot and the load. Passive spring-based arms reduce weight and complexity compared to active manipulators, but their spring-damper dynamics can introduce oscillatory forces that degrade locomotion stability. This paper derives an extended Zero Moment Point (ZMP) formulation that includes passive payload-interface dynamics, relating stiffness, damping, and payload mass to the stability margin. The analysis shows that underdamped configurations can resonate with locomotion harmonics. Based on this insight, we augment a Single Rigid Body Dynamics model with passive subsystem dynamics and integrate it into a Model Predictive Control framework. In simulation, the proposed controller reduces stability violations by up to $10\times$, from $7.0\%$ to $0.7\%$, and increase locomotion efficiency by lowering horizontal ground reaction force effort by up to $15\%$ compared to a nominal baseline. Hardware experiments with a $2\,\mathrm{kg}$ payload show stable locomotion under pull-release disturbances where the nominal controller fails. The same model also enables end-effector tracking through passive arm dynamics without direct arm actuation.

</details>


### [167] [C-ARC: Continuous-Adaptive Range Clustering for Non-Repetitive LiDAR Sensors](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18948)
*Nick B. Schroeder,Jonathan Lichtenfeld,Oskar von Stryk*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: Development of C-ARC, a framework for real-time clustering of point clouds from non-repetitive LiDAR sensors; enables better mobile robotics applications.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To address limitations of current clustering methods tailored for repetitive mechanical LiDAR sensors, especially with the rise of cost-effective non-repetitive LiDAR sensors.

Method: C-ARC utilizes a Continuous-Adaptive Range Clustering framework with a persistent dual-graph over a sliding window to manage point insertion and cluster retrieval, incorporating an adaptive grid resolution mechanism.

Result: C-ARC operates effectively at 20 Hz on standard hardware, improving clustering quality for non-repetitive data and overcoming limitations of existing methods.

Conclusion: C-ARC enhances real-time clustering capabilities, facilitating applications like SLAM and tracking in mobile robotics while addressing the challenges posed by non-repetitive LiDAR scanning patterns.

Abstract: Real-time LiDAR clustering identifies structures in point clouds, which is an essential prerequisite for many mobile robotics algorithms. Current methods are mostly developed for repetitive mechanical LiDAR sensors. Recently, the use of non-repetitive LiDAR sensors is strongly increasing due to their small cost and form factor. Such non-repetitive Risley prism-based sensors violate two key assumptions of repetitive mechanical sensors: structured scan lines and well-defined frame boundaries. Their Rhodonea-curve trajectories produce non-uniform point distributions, and the absence of a rotation cycle renders conventional scan line indexing inapplicable. To meet such new requirements, we developed C-ARC, a Continuous-Adaptive Range Clustering framework that maintains a persistent dual-graph over a sliding window, decoupling high-frequency point insertion from on-demand cluster retrieval. This is crucial for key functionalities like SLAM or tracking. An adaptive range grid resolution mechanism calibrates grid dimensions at initialization using an exponential control loop, balancing the sparsity-collision trade-off without prior knowledge of the scanning pattern. Implemented as an open-sourced single-threaded C++17 library, C-ARC produces real-time cluster output at 20 Hz on commodity hardware for the Livox Mid-360. Evaluation on the Livox Avia identifies unbounded cell occupancy as the primary limitation for sensors with strongly concentrated scan patterns. The adaptive resolution mechanism additionally improves clustering quality for existing grid-based methods on non-repetitive data.

</details>


### [168] [A High-accuracy Event-based Underwater SLAM System](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18951)
*Yifan Peng,Qihang,Liu,Haoying Li,Yuzhe Li,Junfeng Wu,Ziyang Hong*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: This paper presents a novel event-based underwater stereo SLAM system that addresses reliability issues in existing Time Surface methods due to challenging underwater conditions.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: The motivation is to improve event-based SLAM for underwater environments, overcoming challenges of fluctuating velocities, wide stereo baselines, and texture matching failures.

Method: The approach involves designing a structure-aware metric for Time Surface, utilizing Bayesian Optimization for optimal TS generation, and employing a latest-observation-first triangulation mechanism.

Result: The proposed system demonstrates competitive accuracy performance when evaluated extensively on both public datasets and a newly introduced dataset (UWE).

Conclusion: The contributions include a robust new SLAM system and the UWE dataset, which can aid further research in the field.

Abstract: While event cameras offer immense potential for underwater SLAM, existing Time Surface (TS)-based methods prove highly unreliable when deployed underwater. Fluctuating camera velocities severely degrade TS imaging quality, while wide stereo baselines and repetitive underwater textures induce critical matching failures, frequently triggering system failure. To overcome these challenges, we develop the first high-accuracy event-based underwater stereo SLAM system. A structure-aware metric for TS is designed based on structure tensor coherence and gradients to quantitatively evaluate TS structural information density. By decoupling the optimal TS generation into two distinct stages based on system initialization, Bayesian Optimization(BO) first predicts an optimal prior TS sequentially before initialization while we set an asynchronous online local searching method periodically to obtain appropriate TS in real-time during the tracking stage. We use the prior disparity to guarantee precise data association and "latest-observation-first'' triangulation mechanism to realize stable triangulation. As a benchmark for these solutions and a resource for the community, we also contribute UWE, the first high-quality real-world underwater event dataset containing variable camera motions, complex textures and different trajectory features. Extensive evaluations on public datasets and UWE show the competitive accuracy performance of the proposed SLAM system compared to the state-of-the-art event-based method. The code and data will be open-sourced.

</details>


### [169] [Object-Centric Residual RL for Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real VLA Enhancement](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18953)
*Kinam Kim,Namiko Saito,Heecheol Kim,Katsushi Ikeuchi,Jaegul Choo,Yasuyuki Matsushita*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: This paper presents an object-centric residual reinforcement learning (RL) framework that enhances Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models for manipulation tasks, improving their transferability from simulation to real-world applications.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To address the brittleness of VLA models in physical interactions caused by execution errors, aiming to improve their performance with a zero-shot approach in real-world scenarios.

Method: The method involves using a frozen VLA model as a base and training a corrective residual RL policy in simulation with object pose inputs, enabling effective adaptation to real environments without extensive re-training.

Result: The proposed approach increases the success rate of manipulation tasks on a real robot from 42% to 76% in a zero-shot manner, demonstrating significant improvement and reliability in task execution.

Conclusion: This object-centric residual RL framework not only enhances the robustness of VLA models in real-world interactions but also opens avenues for self-improvement of the base model through reused, improved rollouts.

Abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models can generalize across diverse manipulation tasks, but their imitation-learning-based policies remain brittle in precise physical interactions due to compounding execution errors; Can a reinforcement learning policy trained purely in simulation improve the robustness of real-world VLAs zero-shot? Residual RL, which learns a corrective policy on top of a frozen VLA, offers a natural framework, but existing approaches face a fundamental sim-to-real dilemma: privileged-state methods require lossy distillation for deployment; image-based methods suffer from the visual domain gap; and real-world RL is costly and unsafe. We propose an object-centric residual RL framework that refines VLA actions using object poses, enabling a compact observation space that transfers consistently between simulation and reality. To align the two domains, we additionally replay the same teleoperation demonstrations in simulation to train a sim counterpart of the real-world VLA. The residual RL policy is trained only in simulation with pose noise injection and dropout, and transfers zero-shot to the real robot. Across five manipulation tasks on a real Franka Research 3 (FR3) robot, our method improves the success rate from 42% to 76% zero-shot, and the improved rollouts can be further reused to retrain the base VLA for self-improvement without additional teleoperation. Project page: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/articles/object-centric-residual-rl/

</details>


### [170] [TactSpace: Learning a Physics-enriched Shared Latent Space for Tactile Sim-to-Real Transfer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18959)
*Arunim Joarder,Arjun Bhardwaj,René Zurbrügg,Mayank Mittal,Florin Püntener,Sira Bielefeldt,Cosmin Roman,Vaishakh Patil,Marco Hutter*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: This paper introduces a multi-modal representation learning framework for tactile sensing that facilitates zero-shot sim-to-real transfer by aligning diverse tactile modalities in a shared latent space, demonstrating reduced errors in force prediction and shape reconstruction tasks.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Current simulators do not accurately model the mechanics of tactile sensors, impeding effective sim-to-real transfer in robotic applications.

Method: The proposed framework utilizes modality-specific encoders to project various tactile observations into a common embedding space, trained using self- and cross-reconstruction objectives and contrastive alignment.

Result: The model shows zero-shot sim-to-real transfer capabilities, achieving a 16.7% decrease in force prediction error and a 45.8% decrease in shape reconstruction error with the integration of multi-physics simulation modalities.

Conclusion: The framework enhances the transferability of tactile representations across different tasks and facilitates scalable tactile data generation using an efficient simulation model.

Abstract: Tactile sensing provides direct measurements of contact interactions that are essential for robotic manipulation. However, current simulators lack the fidelity to faithfully model the complex deformation and transduction mechanics of tactile sensors, severely hindering sim-to-real transfer in robot learning pipelines. To address this challenge, we propose a multi-modal representation learning framework that aligns heterogeneous tactile modalities within a shared latent space, eliminating the need for accurate raw-signal simulation while preserving relevant contact information. Our approach employs modality-specific encoders to project diverse tactile observations, such as simulated penetration depth and real-world capacitance, into a common embedding space. The model is trained using self- and cross-reconstruction objectives alongside contrastive alignment, encouraging modality-invariant yet information-rich representations. We evaluate the learned embeddings on indenter shape identification, force prediction, and geometric reconstruction tasks, training exclusively in simulation and testing directly on real sensor measurements. Our results demonstrate zero-shot sim-to-real transfer across physically dissimilar representations. Furthermore, incorporating multi-physics simulation modalities yields more informative embeddings that transfer across diverse downstream tasks, demonstrating a 16.7% reduction in force prediction error and a 45.8% reduction in shape reconstruction error. Finally, we release an efficient Warp-based implementation of a penalty-based tactile simulation model for Isaac Lab, enabling scalable tactile data generation.

</details>


### [171] [Congestion-Aware Robot Tour Planning in Crowded Environments](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19031)
*Stefano Bernagozzi,Charlie Street,Masoumeh Mansouri,Lorenzo Natale*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: This paper presents a probabilistic tour planner for autonomous mobile service robots navigating crowded environments, addressing challenges posed by human congestion.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To enhance the performance of robots navigating through crowded spaces, minimizing the negative impact of human presence and collision avoidance maneuvers.

Method: The authors develop a probabilistic tour planner that uses circular linear flow field (CLiFF) maps to predict human trajectories and incorporates these predictions into an online Markov decision process for efficient routing.

Result: Experiments conducted on a real-world crowd dataset in a shopping mall demonstrate the effectiveness and scalability of the proposed approach, allowing robots to re-plan their routes dynamically as new human movements are observed.

Conclusion: The proposed method significantly improves robot navigation in crowded environments by accurately predicting human trajectories and allowing for real-time re-planning.

Abstract: Autonomous mobile service robots are often required to complete tours that require navigating through a set of locations in an environment. Example domains include guiding people through a shopping mall, delivering packages in a fulfilment centre, or giving guided tours in a museum. However, in crowded environments, the presence of people may negatively impact robot performance. For example, humans will activate robot collision avoidance manoeuvres that slow the robot down. Crowds move stochastically and vary throughout the day. In this paper we present a probabilistic tour planner for crowded environments which explicitly reasons over human congestion. We learn circular linear flow field (CLiFF) maps which predict human trajectories given an initial observation. We then use these predictions to build and solve a Markov decision process online which efficiently routes the robot through the environment. Our approach is scalable enough to re-plan as new people are observed. We evaluate our approach on a real-world crowd dataset in a shopping mall.

</details>


### [172] [Sensor Configuration Matters: A Systematic Evaluation of Multimodal SLAM on Quadruped Robots](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19067)
*Roberto Corlito,Fabian Schmidt,Nils Seibert,Markus Enzweiler,Abhinav Valada,Arne Roennau*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: This paper evaluates the impact of sensor configurations on SLAM performance in quadrupedal robots, highlighting the advantages of specific camera setups and inertial integration methods.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To understand how hardware sensor configurations affect SLAM performance during legged locomotion due to unique challenges faced by quadrupedal robots.

Method: A systematic evaluation of visual, visual-inertial, and LiDAR-visual-inertial SLAM methods using the GrandTour dataset on an ANYmal D quadruped, focusing on different camera modalities and inertial sensor configurations.

Result: Hardware selection significantly influences SLAM performance; stereo setups outperform others, global shutter cameras reduce motion-induced failures, and standard inertial integration can degrade vision-based SLAM under aggressive dynamics.

Conclusion: The findings provide design guidelines for selecting sensors to enhance SLAM resilience in agile quadrupedal systems.

Abstract: Autonomous navigation of quadrupedal robots in diverse environments fundamentally relies on resilient Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM). While visual-inertial SLAM has matured across wheeled, handheld, and aerial platforms, a critical evaluation gap remains regarding how hardware-level sensor configurations affect performance under the aggressive dynamics of legged locomotion. Quadrupeds introduce distinct embodiment-induced sensory challenges, including foot-impact shocks, high-frequency mechanical vibrations, and rapid angular rotations, which degrade standard perception pipelines. To address this gap, we present a systematic evaluation of state-of-the-art visual, visual-inertial, and LiDAR-visual-inertial SLAM methods using the GrandTour dataset recorded on an ANYmal D quadruped. We isolate and quantify the impacts of camera modalities, shutter techniques, and inertial sensor tiers, analyzing their trade-offs across localization accuracy, algorithmic robustness, and computational resource utilization. Our empirical findings demonstrate that hardware selection has substantial influence on system resilience: stereo configurations consistently outperform monocular and RGB-D modalities, global shutter cameras significantly mitigate motion-induced tracking failures compared to rolling shutter cameras, and, crucially, standard inertial integration can degrade the performance of primarily vision-based frameworks under harsh legged locomotion. These insights additionally offer concrete design guidelines for tailoring custom sensor payloads to achieve dependable perception on agile legged systems.

</details>


### [173] [ReSiReg: Towards Spatially Consistent Semantics in Language-Conditioned Robotic Tasks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19088)
*Simon Schwaiger,David Seyser,Alessandro Scherl,Wilfried Wöber,Gerald Steinbauer-Wagner*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: This paper introduces ReSiReg to enhance the spatial consistency of VLMs for robotics by using feature reconstruction and clustering approaches, resulting in better performance in dense language-grounded retrieval and real-world manipulations.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Dense VLM embeddings are noisy and lack spatial consistency, which is critical for robotic applications that require reasoning over both semantics and 3D space.

Method: ReSiReg utilizes spatially consistent VLM intermediates, clustering them into visual prototypes, deriving language descriptors, and reconstructing patches as soft mixtures of these prototypes.

Result: Quantitative evaluations on OVSS and 3D mapping show improved performance in dense retrieval, and qualitative assessments demonstrate better spatial consistency in real-world manipulation scenes.

Conclusion: The compact 25M dense VLM introduced is effective for robotic applications and competitive with larger models, indicating a significant advancement in VLM utility for spatial tasks.

Abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) enable robots to follow open-language instructions. However, dense VLM embeddings have shown to be noisy and lack spatial consistency. This is problematic for robotic applications, which require simultaneous reasoning over semantics and 3D space. We examine spatial structure across recent VLMs and propose ReSiReg, a feature reconstruction method that uses spatially consistent VLM intermediates to improve dense language-grounded retrieval. ReSiReg clusters intermediates into visual prototypes, derives their language descriptors, and reconstructs each patch as a soft mixture of prototype-level language embeddings. We evaluate quantitatively on OVSS and 3D mapping across backbones, and qualitatively in real-world manipulation scenes. Quantitative results show improved dense retrieval; manipulation scenes show more spatially consistent target activations. We further provide a compact 25M dense VLM for robotic applications, substantially smaller than and competitive with ViT-B baselines. Available at https://resireg.github.io

</details>


### [174] [ART-VS: Adaptive Resolution Tiling for Vision Transformer Visual Servoing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19089)
*Alessandro Scherl,Bernhard Neuberger,Simon Schwaiger,David Mulero-Pérez,Lucas Muster,Jose Garcia-Rodriguez*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: The paper presents Adaptive Resolution Tiling Visual Servoing (ART-VS), a method that balances robustness and precision in robotic positioning using Vision Transformer features without task-specific training, achieving significantly improved outcomes compared to existing methods.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: The research addresses the trade-off between robustness and precision in robotic visual servoing, aiming to enhance performance while maintaining generalization without the need for extensive training.

Method: ART-VS employs a two-phase approach: a coarse phase utilizing native ViT resolution for stable alignment, followed by a high-resolution phase that focuses on local neighborhood matching to boost accuracy.

Result: ART-VS demonstrates a convergence rate of 95.4% in perturbed conditions, surpassing traditional methods by notable margins, and achieving substantial reductions in positioning error and resource usage.

Conclusion: The method is validated across different ViT backbones, exhibiting superior performance in real-world applications, including effective grasping of novel objects.

Abstract: Visual servoing with self-supervised Vision Transformer (ViT) features enables training-free robotic positioning with strong generalization, but faces a fundamental trade-off between robustness and precision. Coarse patch-level descriptors provide stable correspondences yet limit positioning accuracy. Increasing image resolution improves precision but yields only marginal robustness gains - under perturbation, high-resolution processing improves convergence success rate from 76.6% to just 81.0% despite 12x more ViT patches. Therefore, we propose Adaptive Resolution Tiling Visual Servoing (ART-VS), a two-phase method that adapts feature granularity to servoing progress: a coarse phase at native ViT resolution for stable alignment, then a tiled high-resolution phase that restricts matching to local neighborhoods improving positioning accuracy. Without any task-specific training, ART-VS achieves 95.4% convergence under perturbation, outperforming standard and full-resolution ViT-based servoing by 18.8 and 14.4 percentage points. Over the former it reduces positioning error by 53%, while running at over 10x higher speed and 27% lower VRAM than the latter. We validate ART-VS across three ViT backbones and demonstrate real-world category-level grasping of unseen object instances, achieving 95/100 on transparent bottles and 98/100 on shoes. Code available under https://art-vs.github.io/.

</details>


### [175] [GCNGrasp-VP: Affordance-Guided View Planning for Efficient Task-Oriented Grasping](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19091)
*Zanjia Tong,Wenlong Dong,Chengjie Zhang,Hong Zhang*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: GCNGrasp-VP is a new framework that integrates affordance field prediction with active view planning to improve task-oriented grasping performance under occlusion without scene reconstruction.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: The degradation of grasping performance due to occluded object views and limitations of existing methods that either assume visibility or rely on complex scene reconstruction.

Method: GCNGrasp-VP integrates GCNGrasp-v2 for grasp evaluation and affordance field prediction, alongside the Affordance-guided View Planner that uses these predictions to optimize camera views without scene reconstruction.

Result: The approach significantly surpasses baselines in view planning with a single adjustment and demonstrates higher grasp success rates in real-world tests.

Conclusion: The framework offers efficient, real-time grasping improvements, validating its effectiveness in occluded environments.

Abstract: Task-oriented grasping performance degrades significantly when object views suffer from occlusions. Existing task-oriented grasping methods typically assume task-relevant regions are visible in the initial frame, while view planning approaches enable active perception but often ignore task semantics and rely on time-consuming scene reconstruction. To address these limitations, we present GCNGrasp-VP, an efficient framework integrating affordance field prediction with active view planning. Central to this framework is GCNGrasp-v2, a task-oriented grasp model that simultaneously supports grasp evaluation and affordance field prediction, achieving constant-time inference complexity. Leveraging this capability, our Affordance-guided View Planner (Affordance-VP) utilizes the affordance field as an information gain metric to guide camera observation of task-relevant regions without requiring scene reconstruction. View planning results show that our method significantly outperforms scene-uncertainty-driven baselines with only one view adjustment. Real-world validation further confirms substantial improvements in grasp success rates for single-object scenarios while maintaining millisecond-level computational latency. Code and models are available at https://github.com/Instinct323/GCNGrasp-VP.

</details>


### [176] [Monocular 3D Occupancy Perception for Robots on Sidewalks via Hybrid 2D-3D Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19122)
*Yukai Ma,Joe Lin,Liu Liu,Honglin He,Lulu Ricketts,Brad Squicciarini,Yong Liu,Bolei Zhou*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: WalkOCC is a monocular 3D occupancy perception framework designed for mobile robots on sidewalks, utilizing hybrid methods to improve prediction accuracy and generalization without costly annotations.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: The need for safe navigation of mobile robots in cluttered sidewalk environments, contrasting with existing methods focused on structured road conditions.

Method: WalkOCC integrates geometric grounding from paired LiDAR-RGB data with scalable learning from unpaired monocular images, utilizing pseudo occupancy supervision and image-level representations.

Result: Significant improvements in prediction accuracy, enhanced segmentation of urban structures, and robustness to environmental variations compared to existing self-supervised baselines.

Conclusion: WalkOCC effectively advances sidewalk navigation for robots while introducing the Sidewalk3D dataset for improved evaluation and benchmarking.

Abstract: Sidewalks in the real world are crowded, cluttered, and less structured than roads, making 3D occupancy prediction a key ingredient for the safe navigation of mobile robots such as delivery bots and electric wheelchairs. Existing occupancy learning pipelines are largely designed for on-road autonomous driving and often train on large-scale paired LiDAR-RGB datasets with dense 3D supervision and multiple camera inputs, which are costly to collect and do not adequately capture sidewalk-specific characteristics. We propose WalkOCC, a hybrid Ray-marching monocular 3D occupancy perception framework for robots operating on sidewalks. WalkOCC explicitly couples geometric grounding from LiDAR-RGB paired data with scalable learning from large-scale unpaired monocular images. It bootstraps pseudo occupancy supervision from paired sequences and jointly learns image-level representations on additional 2D-only data. It yields stable optimization and improved generalization without requiring costly 3D occupancy annotations. Extensive experiments demonstrate consistent gains in prediction accuracy, fine-grained segmentation of subtle urban structures such as curbs and gutters, and robustness to environmental and cross-embodiment shifts compared with self-supervised image-based baselines. To facilitate evaluation and benchmarking, we also introduce Sidewalk3D, a large-scale sidewalk perception dataset with LiDAR-camera paired sequences collected across multiple locations and time periods, along with 3D semantic occupancy annotations for evaluation. Code and data will be made available.

</details>


### [177] [Viking Hill Dataset: A Lidar-Radar-Camera Dataset for Detection and Segmentation in Forest Scenes](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19154)
*Vladimír Kubelka,Oleksandr Kotlyar,Unal Artan,Martin Magnusson*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: A new multi-sensor forest dataset includes co-registered 4D imaging radar along with lidar and RGB camera data, providing robust tree perception for autonomous robots under varying seasonal conditions.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To enhance the perception capabilities of autonomous robots operating in forest environments, particularly addressing the limitations of existing datasets that lack imaging radar data.

Method: A mobile robot collected data using FMCW imaging radar, lidar, RGB camera, IMU, and RTK-GNSS in two sessions under different vegetation states, resulting in 3D cuboid annotations.

Result: Baseline semantic segmentation results show radar achieves competitive IoU scores with lidar for dominant classes, but lower scores for geometrically fine structures like tree trunks.

Conclusion: This work provides a comprehensive dataset supporting advancements in mapping, localization, and sensor fusion under forest canopies, and is publicly available.

Abstract: Autonomous robots operating under forest canopies need robust perception of trees and surrounding vegetation across varying seasonal conditions. Existing forestry datasets provide lidar or camera data with per-tree annotations, but none include co-registered 4D imaging radar -- a modality of growing interest for its resilience to visual degradation, surface contamination, and vegetation occlusion. We introduce a multi-sensor forest dataset collected by a mobile robot equipped with a high-resolution FMCW imaging radar, lidar, RGB camera, IMU, and RTK-GNSS. The site was recorded in two sessions under contrasting vegetation states, and 3D cuboid annotations -- including per-tree diameter estimates -- provide shared semantic labels across all three perception modalities. Furthermore, we provide baseline results for semantic segmentation of the radar and lidar point clouds using MinkowskiUNet. Radar achieves IoU scores competitive with lidar for dominant classes (ground 91%, canopy 86%) while lagging on geometrically fine structures such as tree trunks (56% vs. 74%). A cross-modality analysis further compares lidar and radar trunk segmentation against an RGB detection model, and a diameter-stratified evaluation reveals how trunk segmentation quality varies with tree size. Beyond segmentation, the co-registered multi-modal data and RTK-GNSS-aided reference positioning support research in mapping, localization, and sensor fusion under canopy. The dataset and annotation tools are publicly available.

</details>


### [178] [HT-Bench: Benchmarking and Learning Dexterous Full-Hand Tactile Representations with Egocentric Vision](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19161)
*Yuzhe Huang,Jiaping Wu,Jiaming Jiang,Hezhe Lin,Aikebaier Aierken,Yunlong Wang,Kun Cheng,Ziyuan Jiao,Yuanxin Zhong*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: This paper presents HT-Bench, a large-scale benchmark for tactile representation learning, and introduces HandTouch, an advanced encoder that significantly outperforms existing baselines in multiple tactile tasks.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: The paper addresses the need for a universal benchmark in tactile representation learning amid diverse tactile sensor designs and data formats.

Method: Introduces HT-Bench, which consists of 10M RGB and 7.8M tactile frames across 226 tasks, and proposes HandTouch, a vector-quantized vision-tactile encoder for learning representations through progressive training.

Result: HandTouch outperforms baseline tactile encoders, achieving improved Recall@5, reduced RMSE, and increased OOD cIoU in various tasks.

Conclusion: The findings highlight HandTouch's effectiveness and underscore the potential of large-scale egocentric tactile data to enhance tactile representation learning.

Abstract: Establishing a universal benchmark for tactile representation learning in robotic manipulation remains challenging due to the diversity of tactile sensor designs, data formats, and robot embodiments. Rather than seeking to establish such, we explore a scalable and promising direction for future development: egocentric vision paired with full-hand tactile data. To this end, we introduce \textbf{HT-Bench}, a large-scale multi-task benchmark for dexterous full-hand tactile sensing, comprising 10M RGB frames and 7.8M tactile frames collected across 226 tasks. HT-Bench evaluates tactile representations from three key perspectives: whether they encode meaningful contact geometry, whether they can align tactile observations with visual information, and whether they generalize to unseen tasks. To assess these capabilities, HT-Bench includes four tasks: fine-grained tactile similarity retrieval, masked tactile inpainting, vision-to-tactile synthesis, and multimodal tactile frame prediction. We further propose \textbf{HandTouch}, a vector-quantized vision--tactile encoder that learns tactile representations through progressive spatial, cross-modal, and temporal training. Across HT-Bench, HandTouch consistently outperforms representative tactile encoder baselines, improving Recall@5 on fine-grained tactile similarity retrieval from 74.65\% to 85.23\%, reducing RMSE on masked tactile inpainting from 0.022 to 0.010, and increasing OOD cIoU on vision-to-tactile synthesis from 0.628 to 0.705. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of HandTouch and suggest that large-scale egocentric full-hand tactile data provides a scalable basis for evaluating and advancing tactile representation learning in dexterous manipulation.

</details>


### [179] [Hardware- and Vision-in-the-Loop Validation of Deep Monocular Pose Estimation for Autonomous Maritime UAV Flight](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19176)
*Maneesha Wickramasuriya,Beomyeol Yu,Jaden Shin,Mason Huslig,Taeyoung Lee,Murray Snyder*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: This paper introduces a framework for validating autonomous UAV operations on ships using indoor simulations of maritime environments with a focus on pose estimation and control.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
